# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "Pride and His Prisoners" by A. L. O. E. (Gutenberg 60149)

**Frame:** Ch. I–III are a dialogue between two personified spirits on Nettleby Tower's battlements, Somersetshire, Sabbath spring morning. **Intemperance** (wild, red-meteor eyes, gin-palace victims) and **Pride** (taller, darker, deeper voice, "without his veil"). Pride claims he rules via "vinous" (high spirit), "acid" (sourness, suspicion), and final stage fermentation. He disinherited-tempted Hugh Bardon. Pride is near the church, mounts the pulpit, tarnishes offerings. Pride's only fear is the Spirit of the Gospel (David/Goliath). Pride boasts of "Ida Aumerle" as his target. Footnote: the lady/pastor "devil told me the same thing" joke.

**Characters:**
- **Hugh Bardon**: former owner of Nettleby Tower, died; disinherited only son Timon for marrying a farmer's daughter.
- **Timon Bardon, M.D.** (Dr. Bardon): disinherited son, ~60s, long white hair, leonine, black beetling brows, downturned mouth, poor surgeon at **Mill Cottage** (formerly claimed "Milton" by daughter). Favourite axiom: "It's the fool that gets on in the world." Calls people "lion" image; says "No!" sharp; hates Earl of Dashleigh. Sensitive to obligations; keeps mental balance of favours.
- **Cecilia Bardon** ("Cecily"): his daughter, 30–40, sallow, light hair, grey eyes, vain of dress, fawn-coloured kid boots, pink ribbons, guitar, says "Yes" drawn out to three syllables. Overdressed, sings badly (Bel raggio lusinghier).
- **Ida Aumerle**: 18+, dark "gazelle" eyes, pastor's daughter, gentle, sacrificing, Christian. Refused Dashleigh's proposal. Runs classes (Sunday, farm-boys class idea). Her mother died when she was 12.
- **Mabel Aumerle**: younger sister, ~15, small upturned nose, impulsive, proud, "Mabel" plays "porcelain vs crockery" with sisters.
- **Lawrence Aumerle**: the vicar of Ayrley, Ida's father, gentle, peacemaker, prays for Augustine.
- **Mrs. Barbara Aumerle**: second wife (formerly Miss Lambert), practical, stout, high colour, "common sense," scissors, cuts poor clothes, dislikes emotion; overrules girls' walks and balloon.
- **Augustine Aumerle**: Lawrence's younger brother, handsome, brilliant Cambridge, sceptic, German philosophy, Tennyson. Owns Aspendale (Lodge). Friend of Verdon.
- **Reginald, Earl of Dashleigh**: Lord of Dashleigh Hall, twelfth earl, ~mid-life, nervous, proud, giddy on heights (Swiss mountain incident). Dashleigh's pride, "coronet." Proposed to Ida, refused, then married Annabella.
- **Annabella Aumerle**, Countess of Dashleigh: Ida's cousin (mother was Lawrence's late wife's sister), "Titania," writes romance "The Fairy Lake," pen-name "Egeria." Sweet-tempered but proud.
- **Mr. Verdon**: aeronaut, small, sharp features, grey eyes, 15 ascents.
- **Duke of Montleroy**: arrives at Hall at luncheon, witnesses quarrel.
- **Bates**: Annabella's lady's-maid. **Mullins**: coachman (mentioned). **Mills**: lodge-keeper. **Dr. G——**: physician at Cliff Cottage. **Mrs. Clayton**: blind widow, Pelton.
- **Auger / Thomas Auger**: lawsuit winner, owner of Nettleby Tower; dies, wills Tower to Timon.
- **Mrs. Graham, Mrs. Bowman** (minor).

**Events in order:**
1. Ch.I–III: Pride/Intemperance dialogue. Ida "snow-drop." Pride pleased to have Ida.
2. Ch.II: Ida's conversion at 18-ish (night, Bible, joyful tears); refuses Dashleigh's suit; Dashleigh then engaged to Annabella; Mrs. Aumerle marries Lawrence; Ida dethroned.
3. Ch.III: Mrs. Aumerle vetoes Ida's anthem; Ida gives up music. Lawrence's prosperity-induced complacency; wife dies. Augustine sceptic.
4. Ch.IV: Mill Cottage described; Cecilia's fawn boots; Dr. Bardon's card-rack; the crimson curtain gift; Annabella's invitation to Dashleigh Hall.
5. Ch.V: Mabel's "porcelain" talk; Mrs. Aumerle forbids late walks and Ida's farm-boy class; compromise (Mrs. A. takes lads, Ida takes mothers' class... actually Ida takes the lads' class, Mrs. A. the mothers').
6. Ch.VI: Donkey-chaise visit; Dashleigh Hall; Annabella gracious; Venice sumach slip.
7. Ch.VII: Annabella's background; marriage sours; Dashleigh (fallen from horse at donkey's bray), stays for Duke; "Tell that Bardon..." overhears; Bardon's outburst; Annabella weeps.
8. Ch.VIII: Augustine vs Lawrence debate (Psalm 131; "Give me the childish..."); Augustine leaves.
9. Ch.IX: Annabella writes "The Precipice and the Peer" (satire on Dashleigh's Swiss mountain). Dashleigh forbids publication.
10. Ch.X: Mabel and Ida in arbour; "ladder of good works" broken; "bright golden cord."
11. Ch.XI: Balloon talk; Dashleigh reads manuscript, tears it; calls her "insolent girl"; Duke sees; Annabella leaves for vicarage; says "shall sleep at the vicarage."
12. Ch.XII: Chess, Cecilia sings, Mabel asks to go in balloon; "That's pride" (Mrs. A.); Annabella arrives; Bardon declares refusal to meet Dashleigh.
13. Ch.XIII: Mrs. A. vs Mabel; Augustine's mission to Dashleigh (pardon if she apologises); Annabella refuses; Dr. Bardon summoned.
14. Ch.XIV: Bardon's lies (papists, nun, priest); urges Annabella to publish satire. Annabella sends "Precipice" to magazine editor and letter to London publisher (name on title as Countess). Ida's visit refused. Mabel offers to call Bates back; Annabella says "No."
15. Ch.XV: Dashleigh's remorse; sees "Precipice" in magazine; Lawrence's letter; Dashleigh sends note to Augustine asking for balloon place.
16. Ch.XVI: Ida pleads; Mrs. A. rebukes Annabella; Annabella leaves for Bardon's cottage.
17. Ch.XVII: Bardon buys magazine at Pelton library; librarian mentions article; Bardon says "She's done it!"
18. Ch.XVIII: Bardon reads magazine at Mrs. Clayton's; learns of Auger's death (from Times). Annabella arrives at Mill Cottage; Cecilia stitches drugget; Bates annoyed.
19. Ch.XIX: Balloon rumour; Mabel gets Lawrence's leave; Mrs. A.'s "opinion"; Ida undecided.
20. Ch.XX: Morning 12 May; Mabel meets Augustine; Verdon; Dr. Bardon arrives; Dashleigh arrives pale.
21. Ch.XXI: Dashleigh panics, lunges out; "Let go!"; Eaglet floats off; Verdon: "They are lost."
22. Ch.XXII: Valve jammed; rope snaps; cloud; sea-plain; wine-cork pops; Dashleigh fights; whirlwind; Dashleigh faints.
23. Ch.XXIII: Ida's remorse; Ida goes to Mill Cottage with vicar; Bardon brings news; Annabella's curse at Bardon; "never enter my presence."
24. Ch.XXIV: Prayer in balloon (Litany); Mabel's letter dropped; Dashleigh gives Annabella's pocket-book, scribbles two words on blank page (Forgiveness/Peace); "Death is a great preacher"; Augustine can't lead prayer.
25. Ch.XXV: Ida's confession to Mrs. A.; "faults on both sides"; chain broken.
26. Ch.XXVI: Augustine's night meditation; balloon deflates over sea; ballast, instruments, grapples dropped; cut ropes; car ditches; sail sighted, rescued.
27. Ch.XXVII: Telegram "Safe... brain fever... Cliff Cottage, B——, Devon"; Annabella's note to publisher cancels edition; Mrs. A. relents; Mabel's letter returned.
28. Ch.XXVIII: Bardon inherits Nettleby Tower; train to Devon; fisherman's cottage; Dr. G——; station man. Mabel reunited.
29. Ch.XXIX: Augustine conversion; Aumerles return home; countess with Ida at cottage; Dashleigh's pocket-book two words; Annabella reconciled.
30. Ch.XXX: July; Dashleigh recovering; visit to Bardon at Nettleby Tower; handshake; epilogue moralising poem.

**Key quoted phrases:** "The spirit of Pride," "Pride... Tyrant!", "Forgiveness and peace," "pickled..." (none in Book 1 beyond this).

## BOOK 2: "Poppy Ott's Pedigreed Pickles" by Leo Edwards (Gutenberg 71240)

**Characters:**
- **Poppy Ott**: long-legged, long-headed, bold schemer; "president"; calls Jerry "kid," "Jerry, old pal." Son of Mr. Ott (shiftless turned factory manager; ran stilt factory). Mother dead.
- **Jerry Todd** (narrator): "Yours Truly"/Y.T., vice-president, comedic, dislikes pickles after poisoning. Father "Dad," mother "Mother."
- **Mr. Foreman Pennykorn**: president of Canners Exchange Bank, Tutter; tight, grasping; grandpa of Forrest.
- **Norman Pennykorn**: son, runs Tutter Canning Company; **Forrest Pennykorn**: grandson, snob, sporty roadster, mocks boys; "monkey-face" insult.
- **Simon Weckler**: widow/widower, old, grumpy, cane, huge yellow tomcat **Peter**; paid for Scouts' assembly cabin; owns summerhouse playhouse and vacant lot across from canning factory; daughter Clara eloped with Nathan Weir (never heard from).
- **Mrs. Clayton**: his housekeeper.
- **Butch McGinty**: towing/house-mover, bachelor, dirty, mule named **Jerusalem**; secret pickle recipe; burned cookies; hired at $3.50/day; cat sleeps on table.
- **Mrs. Cora O'Mally** ("the pickle woman"): Irish widow, Weir house in river bottoms, 4 bushels sold at $2/bushel; ~700 bushel crop; was paid $1/bushel by canning co; Aunt Jemima pickle recipe source; later marries Uncle Abner.
- **Bill Hadley**: town marshal.
- **Doc Leland**: physician (Lizzie car, nose glasses).
- **Mr. Thomas Lorring**: banker, Commercial Bank, helped stilt factory; big red hand.
- **Mr. Stair**: newspaper editor (Tutter Daily Globe).
- **Mrs. Bagley, Mrs. Brown, Mrs. Morgan, Mrs. Hempline, Mrs. Cook, Mrs. Springer, Mrs. Bowman, Mrs. Clayton**: women.
- **Red Meyers, Denny Kirk, Spider Whickleberry, Bid Stricker**: kids.
- **Silas Hartenbower**: centenarian.
- **Tommy Weir**: grandson of Weckler, runaway's son; cave-dweller, black eyes, tough.
- **Uncle Abner Weir**: old man, nightgown, fringe whiskers, false teeth, cane, Rimtown Ohio; Tommy's uncle.
- **Nathan Weir**: Tommy's father, one-armed cat strangler; robber; shot in arm; died in hospital.
- **Peg-leg Weir**: river pirate, built stone house; gold cucumbers; shot by posse.
- **Mr. Wiggins** (Wiggins & Wakefield, Rockford) & **Henny** (Poppy's Rockford cousin, wholesale grocer).
- **Mr. Samson** (railroad food buyer), **Mr. Lorrimer** (railroad president, dining car).
- **Deacon Pillpopper**: boat livery.
- **Spider Whickleberry**: rigged the iron cat-catcher (from church).

**Events in order:**
1. Poppy proposes Pickle Parlor; Jerry skeptical; Pennykorns' banker talk overheard (Dandy Dills, Ashton plant, $9/ton corn, 50k goal); Forrest mocks; rent $125/mo refused.
2. Poppy's jar of pickles from Presbyterian food sale (Drake's store); Mrs. Clayton's broken jar; Mr. Weckler's cat Peter; playhouse offered for $5/mo or silent partner (pickle payment); Poppy saves Peter from cistern.
3. Shelves, paint yellow/green; partners $50 each; account at Lorring's bank $100; ad "WHOSE PICKLES" (diamonds error from jewelry robbery article, Box 9, Tutter Daily Globe). 63 letters.
4. Editor Stair; women sample; Peoria police chief telegram (diamond robbery); Bill Hadley explains; Jerry hit by broom (woman).
5. Jerry sick from pickles; Dad shoves pickles; "Doc Leland" arrives.
6. Burglar in Poppy's cellar strews pickles; Poppy's ad cleared; Butch McGinty found to be pickle genius (Mrs. O'Mally's recipe); Butch hired $3.50/day; Aunt Jemima scheme.
7. O'Mally's cellar cry (ghost, Peg-leg Weir stories); cucumber patch 4 bushels.
8. Canning truck scene; Poppy/Jerry wash Butch; pickling; Mr. Ott & wedding at Rockford; sample handbill "Aunt Jemima's Pickles."
9. Samples distributed; store moved to Weckler lot; Norman Pennykorn threatens; Poppy's orders; ptomaine poisoning from church stuffed olives (Mrs. Higgins).
10. Money $100 → $32 left; Weckler attacked in library; gold cucumber found in flower bed; one-armed cat strangler.
11. Cat killer strangles cat at church window; Hartenbower's story (iron mold, lead cucumbers).
12. Poppy bought 130 bushels at $2/bushel without money; O'Mally's ghost (tapping); Pennykorn offers 90¢; "ghost"/hidden cellar.
13. Pennykorn threatens; O'Mally refuses; Forrest threatens; ultimatum.
14. Tunnel search; Poppy's creek idea; tunnel; yell; Tom's cave.
15. Midnight: cat killed in chimney secret door; Poppy captures boy Tom Weir (knocked out).
16. Tom's uncle Abner; boat trick; cave; Abner's whiskers, Bible; Tom's mother story; Tom's grandpa.
17. Abner's story: Peg-leg Weir's gold cucumber key; Nathan's wife; gold stolen; alliance (fifty-fifty incl. O'Mally).
18. Pickling recipe: O'Mally's pickles; church women; Lorring loan $500 at 6%; "Pedigreed Pickles."
19. Church women; cucumbers; Pennykorn's letter to dealers; farmer's cucumbers; Pennykorn offer; Poppy's counter-offer at bank; Poppy sells to Chicago hotels/railroad (Lorrimer, Samson); orders >$6,000.
20. Tom & Weckler; grandfather reunion; gold cucumber halves; key pictures (full moon, clock midnight, chimney, coffin); dig in chimney shadow; treasure chest found (35,000 total).
21. Lorring; Pennykorn stock; Pennykorn agreement; new pickle company; Mrs. O'Mally, Abner, Tom; Nathan's fate; cat-strangler Nathan dies; next book hint: "Poppy Ott and the Freckled Goldfish."

**Key quoted phrases:** "Pickles is pickles." "Poppy's Pickle Parlor... the home of perfect pickles." "Aunt Jemima's Pickles." "Pedigreed Pickles." "What is home without a freckled goldfish?"
